title: Traffic Entropy Detection and Decomposition Playbook
summary: Post-incident playbook proposing detection based on request entropy and rapid decomposition into request cohorts. Goal: enable targeted, low-friction mitigations during credential/traffic floods without broad customer impact.
incident_context: Observed sudden 8x increase in inbound token-generation requests to /v1/generate over 13 minutes on 2026-02-22. Standard rate limits were reached for several tenants; initial WAF rule set blocked obvious bad UA strings but failed to reduce request velocity. Multiple keys suspected leaked from single downstream partner; traffic showed low per-request variance (identical prompt shapes) suggesting automation.
hypotheses: Low request entropy (very similar request signatures) signals scripted/key-sharing botnets vs organic traffic.
Decomposing traffic into cohorts (by prompt-hash, UA fingerprint, region, product-route) enables surgical throttles with minimal collateral damage.
A dynamic ladder of rate ceilings per cohort (progressive, data-driven) reduces cost and SLO impact more than binary global blocking.
WAF rules that are too coarse cause customer errors; choreography between WAF + rate ladders + key quarantine is required.
Entropy collapse (sudden drop in signature diversity) is a leading indicator of credential stuffing events.
detection_signals: per-route unique-prompt-hash per-minute (baseline vs current) > 5x drop in diversity
Gini coefficient of request fingerprints increasing beyond threshold
median request size and token distribution clustering into <3 modes
rise in 429/401 errors correlated to a narrow set of API keys
sudden bloom in single UA + single region + identical prompt structure
playbook_steps_oncall: 1) Triage: Pull 15-min window of inbound requests to /v1/*; compute entropy by prompt-hash, UA, ip_subnet. (dashboard: entropy-panel)
2) Attribution: If >70% of traffic maps to <=3 prompt-hash clusters and <=5 API keys, mark event as low-entropy storm and escalate to SRE lead.

3) Immediate mitigations (safe-first): a) Apply cohort-level soft-rate-limits: 50% of baseline to top cohort; b) Enable temporary request sampling & record-full-headers; c) Add temporary 403 challenge for unknown UA patterns for 5 minutes.
4) WAF choreography: Do NOT apply broad IP blocks. Instead deploy 1 targeted custom rule matching cohort fingerprints (prompt-hash / UA / route) staged at 5% canary then 50% then 100% if effective.

5) Key actions: Identify top API keys by request volume; mark suspected keys read-only in dashboard, notify Customer Success for possible rotation; create temporary key quarantine policy for keys with >90% malicious-cohort mapping.
6) Observe: Monitor p50/p95 latency, error rate, cost-per-minute. If collateral customer errors > 2% of affected tenants, rollback WAF rule and widen sampling.
7) Post-incident: Run clustering offline to validate cohort boundaries and produce fingerprints for automated future blocking.

8) Communication: Post initial incident note to #sre-incident with summary, keys impacted, and mitigation steps. Notify affected partners via CS if partner keys implicated. Prepare customer-facing blurb if any paid tenants experienced degraded availability.
debugging_checklist: Extract top 200 prompt-hashes and sample 10 requests from each
Collect UA strings, accept-language, content-length, geo, ASNs for top cohorts
Check KV cache hit rate changes (eviction spikes) correlated with cohorts
Run rate-limit backfill queries to see when quotas were first reached per key
Verify WAF logs for any rule matches and false-positive indicators
mitigation_templates: Cohort soft-limit: rate_limit(c) = max(5rpm, 0.5 * baseline(c)) for 10 minutes
WAF rule template: match(prompt_hash IN [..] AND ua_string IN [..] AND route = '/v1/generate') ACTION count/ban/loggable
Key quarantine note template for CS: 'We observed automated traffic patterns on your API key; we've temporarily limited throughput pending rotation. Contact SRE if you need assistance.'
experiments_to_run: A/B test: cohort ladder vs global throttle on synthetic low-entropy floods (simulated) measuring user-visible errors
Entropy alert tuning: evaluate precision/recall for thresholds over past 12 months of traffic; tune to target false positive rate 0.25%
Auto-cohorting: pipeline that computes prompt-hash clusters in streaming infra and exposes top-5 cohorts to oncall UI
decisions: Adopt entropy-based alert as a primary detection signal for credential flooding incidents.
Prioritize development of cohort soft-limits in the serving runtime (Q2 2026).
WAF changes must be staged via canary: no direct global IP blocks without SRE + product sign-off.
Create an SRE-CS rotation playbook for partner key compromises.

open_questions_and_risks: How to compute prompt-hash deterministically while preserving PII and privacy? (must redact before hashing)
Can cohort soft-limits be bypassed by simple UA fuzzing? Need combining signals (geo + hash + rate) for robustness
Risk of overfitting cohort rules from one incident causing missed future attack patterns
Operational cost to maintain canary WAF rollouts during high-churn incidents
notes: This doc is a working draft intended for SRE review and a short tabletop exercise. The core idea is to treat low-entropy storms as a separate class of incident and provide a lightweight set of mitigations that reduce cost and maintain customer availability. Keep language intentionally pragmatic: prefer reversible, measurable changes over aggressive blocks.
